content: 1. The concurrent use of hyoscyamine and umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled can lead to an increase in toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. It is recommended to avoid this combination or consider alternative medications. The simultaneous use of these agents with other anticholinergic-containing drugs may result in additive anticholinergic adverse effects. Close monitoring is advised. 2. Both hyoscyamine and vecuronium reduce cholinergic effects and transmission. Caution is advised when using these drugs together, and close monitoring is necessary. 3. Hyoscyamine decreases the levels of ziprasidone by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction is specific to the oral forms of both agents. Additionally, hyoscyamine reduces ziprasidone levels through pharmacodynamic antagonism, while ziprasidone enhances the effects of hyoscyamine via pharmacodynamic synergism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended when these drugs are used together. Additive anticholinergic effects and potential hypoglycemia may occur. 4. Hyoscyamine decreases the levels of zotepine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Hyoscyamine also reduces zotepine levels through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and close monitoring are advised when these drugs are co-administered. 5. Regarding pregnancy, hyoscyamine is classified as Category C, meaning risk to the fetus cannot be ruled out. For lactation, both hyoscyamine and methenamine are excreted in human breast milk, and caution should be exercised when prescribing these medications to breastfeeding women. In contrast, drugs classified as Category A are generally considered acceptable, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk.
